name: Liṅga-initiation (liṅgadīkṣā)
method_summary: The guru, with assistants, bathes the disciple with water from pots consecrated by the five brahma-mantras, whispers the five-syllable mantra secretly into the right ear, installs a purified liṅga in the disciple's life-breath and places it in his hand to be worn for life. In Liṅgāyata practice it is given to all, women and children included.
prerequisites: a qualified guru (SSM 6.1–6); the disciple's discernment and dispassion

name: Wearing the liṅga (liṅgadhāraṇa)
method_summary: The iṣṭaliṅga, kept in a small casket (karaḍige) on a cord, is worn on the body at all times — at the head, throat, chest, armpit, belly or in the hand, never below the navel; inwardly the liṅga of light is held in the mind at the base, heart or brows.

warnings.text: Never separate the liṅga from the body at any time or place.
Wearing it below the navel is a cause of sin; not on the tip of matted hair, lower back or an unclean place.
The text treats the liṅga's accidental fall with the utmost gravity (recorded as restricted).

name: Worship of the iṣṭaliṅga on the palm
method_summary: Daily worship of one's own liṅga held on the left palm (karapīṭha) with water, ash, flowers and the like, without invocation or dismissal because Śiva already abides in it; the palm-worship is ranked above worship on an outer pedestal.

warnings.text: Never abandon liṅga-worship, even at the loss of possessions or life.

name: Gazing on the iṣṭaliṅga (liṅga-yoga)
method_summary: Holding the liṅga on the palm at eye level and gazing on it steadily, then turning the gaze inward to the liṅga within; taught in modern Śivayoga training and associated in legend with the 'unblinking' (animiṣa) yogi.

equivalents.note: fixed gazing on an object; here the object is the worn liṅga and the practice is devotional

notes: Recorded from general knowledge of the Śivayoga revival (Hānagal Kumāra Svāmi); textual source to be found.

name: Contemplation of the inner liṅga of light
method_summary: Continuous contemplation of the jyotirliṅga at the base, in the heart or between the brows — gold, coral-red and crystal respectively — and setting the breath in the liṅga and the liṅga in the breath with a still mind.
signs_of_progress: loss of taste for the outer (SSM 6.44)
the liṅga shines within like a lamp (SSM 12.8)

name: Inner worship with offerings of feeling (bhāva-pūjā)
method_summary: Worship of the inner liṅga of consciousness in the heart-shrine with inner offerings — forbearance as bath, discrimination as cloth, truth as ornament, dispassion as garland, samādhi as scent, freedom from ego as rice, faith as incense, knowledge as lamp, the world as food-offering, silence as bell.

equivalents.note: inner worship with mental offerings; here directed to the prāṇaliṅga and ranked above ritual worship

name: Śivayoga-samādhi
method_summary: Through inner worship, meditation on Śiva as one's self: the supreme self is contemplated in the haṃsa form with the feeling 'I am He' until attention is undivided; the six centres are contemplated from the base to the brows and Śambhu in the aperture called Kailāsa within the thousand-petalled lotus.

warnings.text: The breath element (meeting of prāṇa and apāna) is done on the teacher's instruction (commentary on 12.6); no method is recorded here.

name: Repetition of the five-syllable mantra
method_summary: Repetition of 'namaḥ śivāya' (six-syllabled with Oṃ) received at initiation, spoken, whispered or — best — mentally, after three breath-restraints, facing east or north and contemplating Śiva in the heart; also used in worshipping the liṅga.

warnings.text: Vows of living on water or air and other emaciating austerities do not reach Śiva's world.

name: Wearing sacred ash (vibhūti) and tripuṇḍra
method_summary: Applying ash consecrated with 'namaḥ śivāya' as three horizontal lines on the forehead and fifteen places of the body; one of the eight shields.

name: Ash-bath (bhasma-snāna)
method_summary: Bathing the body in ash with the five brahma-mantras — the 'fire-bath' ranked above water-baths and enjoined for ascetics.

name: Wearing rudrākṣa
method_summary: Wearing rudrākṣa beads of specified faces and numbers on the crown, head, throat, arms and wrists; one of the eight shields; at death rudrākṣa-water is drunk while thinking of Rudra.

name: Receiving pādōdaka
method_summary: Receiving as sacrament the water in which the feet of the guru or jaṅgama have been washed; one of the eight shields.

name: Receiving prasāda
method_summary: Eating only what has first been offered to the liṅga, and receiving the prasāda of guru and jaṅgama, for purity of mind.

name: Offering all enjoyment to the liṅga (arpaṇa)
method_summary: Whatever is set aside for one's own enjoyment — food, sights, sounds — is first offered to the liṅga and then received as its grace.

name: Service and worship of the jaṅgama
method_summary: Honouring, feeding and serving the wandering Śivayogins (jaṅgamas), whose sight, touch and worship sanctify, and giving them the fruits of one's work.

name: Kāyaka — work as worship
method_summary: Each devotee earns a living by honest work in his or her own occupation, done as worship, not interrupted even for worship, and not gathering beyond the day's need.

name: Dāsōha — sharing the fruit of work
method_summary: Giving what one earns by kāyaka to the jaṅgamas and the community in the spirit 'I am your servant'; in the modern maṭhas, free feeding and schooling.

name: Inner and outer purity (Basava's seven restraints)
method_summary: Not stealing, not killing, not lying, not raging, not despising others, not praising oneself and not blaming others — Basava's definition of inner and outer purity.

name: Observance of the five codes (pañcācāra)
method_summary: Living by liṅgācāra, sadācāra, śivācāra, bhṛtyācāra and gaṇācāra: exclusive worship of the liṅga, honest life, equality of devotees, humility and defence of the community.

name: The three gifts (sopādhi, nirupādhi, sahaja dāna)
method_summary: Giving with a purpose, giving without a purpose, and innate (natural) giving — the last three sub-sthalas of the bhakta-sthala; skill in pure, innate giving marks the passage to māheśvara.

name: The fivefold Śiva-sacrifice
method_summary: Austerity as drying the body for Śiva, action as Śiva's worship, japa as the five syllables or praṇava, meditation, and knowledge as the meaning of the Śiva Āgamas — each replacing its Vedic counterpart.

name: Śivānubhava — shared discourse on experience
method_summary: Devotees gather to speak from and test their experience of Śiva in dialogue, as the śaraṇas did in the Anubhava Maṇṭapa; continued in modern maṭhas as 'śivānubhava' gatherings.

name: Burial of the dead as liṅgaikya
method_summary: The dead devotee, having become one with the liṅga, is buried seated with the liṅga in hand rather than cremated; no death-pollution or ancestral rites are observed.
notes: Community practice from general knowledge; verify the details (posture, rites) in Phase C.
